extracted.intended_audience: federal agency rulewriters, drafters of notices/proposed rules, and Office of the Federal Register staff
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, formatting, and procedural requirements for preparing notices, proposed rules, codification, authority citations, and incorporations by reference for publication in the Federal Register and codification in the Code of Federal Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codification as CFR amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: When codifying, the agency shall draft it as an amendment to the Code of Federal Regulations, in accordance with this subchapter, before submitting it to the Office of the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any document subject to codification must be prepared as a CFR amendment and conform to the organizational/formatting provisions in part 21.

rubrics_metrics.name: Words of issuance and amendatory language
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency that prepares a document that is subject to codification shall include words of issuance and amendatory language that precisely describes the relationship of the new provisions to the Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendatory language must precisely describe how the new provisions relate to existing CFR material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of expiration of codified material
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a codified regulation expires after a specified period by its own terms or by law, the issuing agency shall submit a notification by document for publication in the FEDERAL REGISTER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must notify the Federal Register when codified material expires on its own terms or by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles and subtitles (Code structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: The major divisions of the Code are titles, each of which brings together broadly related Government functions; subtitles may be used to distinguish between materials from an overall agency and its components or to group chapters within a title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use titles for broad functions; use subtitles to separate agency components or group chapters as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapters and subchapters assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapters are assigned to various agencies within a title descriptive of the subject matter; subchapters may be used to group related parts within a chapter; chapter and subchapter assignments are made by the Office of the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies do not unilaterally assign chapter/subchapter designations; coordinate with the Office of the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parts, subparts, and undesignated center heads
rubrics_metrics.description: Parts are unified bodies of regulations applying to a specific function or subject matter; subparts or undesignated center heads may group related sections within a part or subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize related sections under parts and use subparts/center heads to group internal structure for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sections as basic units
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections are the normal divisions of a part and are the basic units of the Code; sections may be divided into paragraphs and further subdivided using lettering indicated in § 21.11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat each section as a self-contained regulatory unit and structure internal subdivisions per the prescribed paragraph lettering sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard organization and numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard organization consists of: (a) Titles numbered in Arabic; (b) Subtitles lettered in capitals; (c) Chapters numbered in Roman capitals; (d) Subchapters lettered in capitals; (e) Parts numbered in Arabic; (f) Subparts lettered in capitals; (g) Sections numbered in Arabic throughout each part (section numbers include part number and section number); (h) Paragraph levels designated as (a),(1),(i),(A),(1),(i) through six levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the exact numbering and lettering conventions (including section format e.g., § 21.15) to ensure consistency and machine/readable structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reservation of numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Where related parts or sections are grouped under a heading, numbers may be reserved at the end of each group to allow for expansion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve numbers proactively within grouped headings to accommodate future additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deviations from standard organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Any deviation from standard CFR designations must be approved in advance by the Office of the Federal Register; requests must be submitted in writing at least five working days before submission of the final rule and include a copy of the final rule document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek written OFR approval at least five working days in advance; Director may allow special keying of section numbers only when it benefits both agency and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required document headings
rubrics_metrics.description: Each rule and proposed rule document submitted to the Office of the Federal Register shall contain the following headings, when appropriate, on separate lines in the following order: (1) Agency name; (2) Subagency name; (3) Numerical references to the CFR title and parts affected; (4) Agency numbers or identifying symbol in brackets, if used; (5) Brief subject heading describing the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these headings in order, each on separate lines; each CFR section in regulatory text shall have a brief descriptive heading preceding the text on a separate line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables of contents requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A table of contents shall be used at the beginning of the part whenever a new part is introduced, an existing part is completely revised, or a group of sections is revised or added and set forth as a subpart or otherwise separately grouped under a center head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the table after the part heading and before regulatory text; list subparts, center headings, sections, and appendix headings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of part headings
rubrics_metrics.description: Each part heading shall indicate briefly the general subject matter of the part; phrases not descriptive of subject matter (e.g., 'Regulations under the Act of July 28, 1955') and introductory expressions like 'Regulations governing' or 'Rules applicable to' may not be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concise descriptive headings that identify subject matter; avoid boilerplate, non-descriptive phrases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments: identification and extent
rubrics_metrics.description: Each amendatory document shall identify in specific terms the unit amended and the extent of the changes made; the number and heading of each section amended shall be set forth in full on a separate line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify precisely what is amended and to what extent; present each amended section number and heading in full on its own line for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: References: specificity and Code citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each reference to the Code of Federal Regulations shall be in terms of the specific titles, chapters, parts, sections, and paragraphs involved; ambiguous references such as 'herein', 'above', 'below', and similar expressions may not be used. Each document that contains a reference to material published in the Code shall include the Code citation as a part of the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit, specific CFR citations (title/part/section/paragraph) rather than vague cross-references; include the Code citation whenever referencing codified material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication in full text; cross-reference exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall publish its own regulations in full text. Cross-references to the regulations of another agency may not be used as a substitute for publication in full text, unless the Office of the Federal Register finds that the regulation meets any of the listed exceptions (court order/statute/Executive order/reorganization plan; exclusive legal authority of another agency; reference is informational/improves clarity; reference to Federal agency test methods/consensus standards that have replaced private methods; reference to Department level from a subagency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish full regulatory text unless an explicit exception applies; consult OFR to determine whether cross-reference substitution is allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel citations of CFR and Federal Register
rubrics_metrics.description: For parallel reference, the Code of Federal Regulations and the FEDERAL REGISTER may be cited in the following forms, as appropriate: 'lll CFR lll (lll FR lll). § lll' or other specified appropriate formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the prescribed parallel citation forms when citing both CFR and FR entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document subject to codification shall include a clear statement as to the date or dates upon which its contents become effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state effective date(s) in the document to avoid ambiguity for implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB control numbers display
rubrics_metrics.description: To display OMB control numbers in agency regulations, those numbers shall be placed parenthetically at the end of the section or displayed in a table or codified section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place OMB control numbers consistently—parenthetical at section end, or in a table/codified section—so they are clearly associated with the regulatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority citations: completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Each section in a document subject to codification must include, or be covered by, a complete citation of the authority under which the section is issued, including general or specific authority delegated by statute and executive delegations, if any, necessary to link the statutory authority to the issuing agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure authority citations show the full chain of statutory and delegated authority linking the law to the issuing agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency responsibility for authority citation accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Each issuing agency is responsible for the accuracy and integrity of the citations of authority in the documents it issues. Each issuing agency shall formally amend the citations of authority in its codified material to reflect any changes therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and formally update authority citations when statutory or delegated authorities change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director exceptions to citation placement/form
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Federal Register may make exceptions to the requirements relating to placement and form of citations of authority whenever the Director determines that strict application would impair the practical use of the citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If strict rules would impair practical use, consult OFR—Director may allow exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of authority citations depending on amendment type
rubrics_metrics.description: If a document sets out an entire CFR part, the agency shall place the complete authority citation directly after the table of contents and before the regulatory text. If amending only certain sections, present the complete authority citation to this part as the first item in the list of amendments; if the authority for issuing an amendment is the same as the authority listed for the whole part, simply restate it; if it changes the authority for the whole part, revise the authority citation in its entirety and may specify particular authority under which certain sections are amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use centralized authority citation placement (end of table of contents or after each subpart heading); specify section-specific authorities within centralized citation as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstatutory authority placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Citation to a nonstatutory document as authority shall be placed after the statutory citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order authority citations with statutory first, then nonstatutory authorities (e.g., E.O.s, FR notices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of formal authority citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal citations of authority shall be in the shortest form compatible with positive identification and ready reference. The Office of the Federal Register shall assist agencies in developing model citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep authority citations concise but uniquely identifiable; request OFR model citations if useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory material citation rules (U.S. Code, Public Laws)
rubrics_metrics.description: All citations to statutory authority shall include a United States Code citation, where available. Citations to titles of the U.S. Code may be cited without Public Law or U.S. Statutes at Large citation; citations to Public Laws and U.S. Statutes at Large are optional when the U.S. Code is cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer US Code citations; include Public Law/Statutes at Large citations when appropriate or when US Code unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstatutory materials citation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonstatutory documents shall be cited by document designation and by FEDERAL REGISTER volume and page, followed, if possible, by the parallel citation to the Code of Federal Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite nonstatutory authorities with FR volume/page and parallel CFR cite where applicable for ready reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name of issuing agency and subdivision for notices
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of the agency issuing a notice shall be placed at the beginning of the document. Whenever a specific bureau, service, or similar unit issues a notice, the name of that bureau, service, or unit shall be placed on a separate line below the name of the agency. File/docket numbers or similar identifying symbols shall be placed in brackets immediately below the other headings. A suitable short title identifying the subject shall be provided on a separate line immediately after other required captions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure notice headings with agency then subagency (if any), then bracketed docket/file numbers, then short title—each on separate lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority citation in notices
rubrics_metrics.description: The authority under which an agency issues a notice shall be cited in narrative form within the text or in parentheses on a separate line following text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the authority for notices plainly either within narrative or on a separate line in parentheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed rules: statement of public rulemaking proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposed rule required by section 553 of title 5 or any other statute, and any similar document voluntarily issued by an agency shall include a statement of the time, place, and nature of public rulemaking proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always state when/where/how the public may participate in rulemaking for proposed rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed rules: reference to authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rules must include reference to the authority under which the regulatory action is proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the statutory or delegated authority underpinning the proposed regulation in the proposed rule document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code designation for proposed rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The area of the Code of Federal Regulations directly affected by a proposed regulatory action shall be identified by placing the appropriate CFR citation immediately below the name of the issuing agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the CFR citation (title and part) directly under the agency name to identify the affected regulatory area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codification conformity for proposed rule full-text
rubrics_metrics.description: Any part of a proposed rule document that contains the full text of a proposed regulation shall also conform to the pertinent provisions of part 21 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If including full regulatory text in a proposed rule, ensure the text follows part 21 formatting and structural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference: policy and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporation by reference is intended to make matter reasonably available to affected persons when incorporated with the Director's approval; incorporation is limited to the edition approved and future amendments/revisions are not included. The Director will apply part 51 standards fairly and uniformly and publication in the FEDERAL REGISTER does not by itself constitute Director approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that incorporation attaches only to the approved edition; do not assume automatic approval by publishing—obtain Director approval when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director approval for incorporation by reference (conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director will informally approve proposed incorporations when the preamble of a proposed rule meets the requirements; the Director will formally approve incorporation in a final rule when: (1) the publication is eligible; (2) the preamble meets requirements; (3) the language of incorporation meets requirements; (4) the publication is on file with the Office of the Federal Register; and (5) the Director has received a written request from the agency. The Director will notify the agency of approval/disapproval within 20 working days after all requirements are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satisfy all five conditions (eligibility, preamble, language, file copy, written request) to obtain formal approval; expect a 20-working-day response window after submission of complete request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency request procedures for incorporation approval
rubrics_metrics.description: For a proposed rule, the agency must: (1) discuss in the preamble how materials are reasonably available to interested parties or how it worked to make them available; and (2) summarize the material proposed to be incorporated. For a final rule, the agency must send a written request letter at least 20 working days before submission, discuss availability in the preamble, summarize the incorporated material, send a copy of the final rule using the proper language of incorporation, and ensure a copy of the incorporated material is on file at the Office of the Federal Register. Agencies may consult OFR at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For final-rule approval, submit a formal package (letter, preamble discussion, summary, proper incorporation language, file copy) at least 20 working days before submitting the final rule for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria for incorporation by reference
rubrics_metrics.description: A publication is eligible for incorporation if it: (a) conforms to the policy in § 51.1; (b)(i) is published data/criteria/standards/specifications/techniques/illustrations or similar material and (ii) does not detract from the usefulness of the FEDERAL REGISTER publication system; and (c) is reasonably available to and usable by the class of persons affected (Director will consider completeness, ease of handling, and whether it is bound, numbered, and organized).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publications should be complete, well organized, and reasonably available; avoid incorporating materials that are not usable or that would undermine FR system usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption against agency-produced publications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director will assume that a publication produced by the same agency seeking approval is inappropriate for incorporation by reference, though such a publication may be approved if it meets eligibility requirements and possesses other unique or highly unusual qualities or cannot be printed using the FEDERAL REGISTER/CFR printing system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to justify why an agency-produced document should be incorporated (unique necessity, printing constraints, or other compelling reasons).

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials not appropriate for incorporation
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials not appropriate for incorporation by reference include: (1) material previously published in the FEDERAL REGISTER; and (2) material published in the United States Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not incorporate material already published in FR or the U.S. Code—these are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper language of incorporation
rubrics_metrics.description: Language incorporating a publication by reference must be precise, complete, and clearly state that incorporation by reference is intended and completed by the final rule; it must: (1) use the words 'incorporated by reference'; (2) state title, date, edition, author, publisher, and number of the publication; (3) inform the user that the incorporated publication is a requirement; (4) make an official showing that the publication is available and how copies may be examined and readily obtained with maximum convenience to the user; and (5) refer to 5 U.S.C. 552(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full bibliographic details and availability information; explicitly use the 'incorporated by reference' phrase and cite 5 U.S.C. 552(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble and DATES caption requirements for approved incorporations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director approves a publication for incorporation by reference in a final rule, the agency must include, under the DATES caption of the preamble, language indicating the Director's approval date (e.g., 'The incorporation by reference ... is approved by the Director of the Federal Register as of llll'), meet the preamble requirements in § 51.5(b), and include 'incorporation by reference' in the list of index terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When incorporating approved publications, include the Director-approval language under DATES, satisfy preamble summary/availability requirements, and add the term to index subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing or removing an approved incorporation
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency seeking approval for a change to an incorporated publication must: (1) publish notice of the change in the FEDERAL REGISTER and amend the Code of Federal Regulations; (2) ensure a copy of the amendment or revision is on file at the Office of the Federal Register; and (3) notify the Director in writing that the change is being made. If a regulation containing an incorporation fails to become effective or is removed from the CFR, the agency must notify the Director in writing within 5 working days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified steps and timelines to change/remove incorporated materials; maintain file copies at OFR and timely notify the Director of removals/failures to take effect.
